(Surah At-Takwir)
Twenty-nine verses, Meccan

In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

﴿When the sun is wound up﴾

In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

﴿When the sun is wound up﴾

Know that He, exalted is He, mentioned twelve things and said: when these things occur, then ﴿a soul will know what it has brought forth﴾ (al-Takwir 81:14). The first is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When the sun is wound up﴾. As for *takwir* (winding up, folding), there are two interpretations.

The first: *takwir* means wrapping in the manner of rotation, like winding a turban (*kawr al-'imama*). In a hadith: "We seek refuge in God from *al-hawr* after *al-kawr*," meaning from scattering after togetherness. *Al-tayy* (folding), *al-laff* (wrapping), *al-kawr* and *al-takwir* are one and the same. The launderer's bundle (*kara al-qassar*) is called *kara* because he gathers his garments into one cloth. Now, that which is wrapped is undoubtedly hidden from the eyes, so by *takwir* He expressed the removal of light from the body of the sun and making it absent from the eyes. For this reason some said: *kuwwirat* means it was obliterated; others said: it was eclipsed; al-Hasan said: its light was effaced; and al-Mufaddal ibn Salama said: *kuwwirat* means its light went away, as if it had concealed itself in a bundle.

The second interpretation: it is said, "I *kawwartu* the wall and *dahwartuhu*," when you throw it down until it falls. Al-Asma'i said: it is said, "He struck him and *kawwarahu*," when he knocked him down. So His saying, ﴿When the sun is wound up﴾, means it was thrown down and cast off from the sphere (*falak*).

There is a third view, reported from Umar, that it is a word derived from Persian, for a blind man is called *kur* (in Persian).

Here are two questions.

The first question: is the raising of *al-shams* (the sun) by way of inception (*ibtida'*, as the subject of a nominal sentence) or by way of agency (*fa'iliyya*, as subject of a verbal sentence)? The answer: rather, it is in the agentive case, its agent being a hidden verb, which *kuwwirat* explains, because *idha* (when) requires a verb after it, since it carries the meaning of a conditional.

The second question: it is narrated that al-Hasan sat in Basra with Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman, and he related from Abu Hurayra that he (peace be upon him) said: "The sun and the moon are two bulls wound up in the Fire on the Day of Resurrection." Al-Hasan said: "And what is their sin?" He said: "I am relating to you from the Messenger of God." So al-Hasan fell silent. The answer: al-Hasan's objection is invalid, because the sun and the moon

are inanimate objects, so casting them into the Fire is not a cause of harm to them. Perhaps this will become a cause for increasing the heat in Hell, so this report is not contrary to reason.

**Second:** His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And when the stars are scattered﴾, meaning they scatter and fall, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And when the planets are dispersed﴾ [al-Infitar: 2]. The original meaning of *inkidar* (انكدار) is *inṣibab* (انصباب, pouring down). Al-Khalil said: It is said *inkadara 'alayhim al-qawm* (انكدر عليهم القوم) when people come in successive groups and pour down upon them. Al-Kalbi said: On that day the sky will rain down stars, so no star will remain in the sky without falling onto the surface of the earth. ʿAta' said: That is because they are in lamps suspended between heaven and earth by chains of light, and those chains are in the hands of the angels. When those in the heavens and the earth die, those chains fall from the hands of the angels.

**Third:** His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And when the mountains are set in motion﴾, meaning removed from the surface of the earth, as in His saying: ﴿And the mountains will be set moving, and they will become a mirage﴾ [al-Naba': 20], or moved through the air, as in His saying: ﴿You will see them passing like the passing of clouds﴾ [al-Naml: 88].

**Fourth:** His saying: ﴿And when the pregnant camels are left neglected﴾. On this there are two opinions.

The first opinion, which is the well-known one: *al-ʿishār* (العشار) is the plural of *ʿushrāʾ* (عشراء), like *nifās* (نفاس) is the plural of *nufasāʾ* (نفساء). It refers to a she-camel in whose pregnancy ten months have passed; then this name applies to her until she gives birth at the completion of the year. She is the most precious thing to her people and the dearest to them. As for ﴿left neglected﴾ (عطلت), Ibn ʿAbbas said: Its people will abandon them because of the terrors of the Day of Resurrection that have come upon them. Nothing was more beloved to the Arabs than pregnant she-camels, and the Arabs were addressed with the matter of the pregnant camels because most of their wealth and livelihood came from camels. The purpose of this is the loss of wealth, the annulment of possessions, and people being preoccupied with themselves, as He said: ﴿The day when neither wealth nor children will benefit, except one who comes to Allah with a sound heart﴾ [al-Shuʿara': 88–89], and He said: ﴿And you have certainly come to Us alone, as We created you the first time﴾ [al-Anʿam: 94].

The second opinion: *al-ʿishār* is a metaphor (kināya, كناية) for the clouds, which are left empty of the water in them. Although this is a metaphor, it is more fitting with the other things mentioned before it. Also, the Arabs liken the clouds to the pregnant woman, and Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And those who carry burdens, a heavy load﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 2].

**Fifth:** His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾. Every land animal that is not domesticated is a *waḥsh* (وحش, wild beast), and the plural is *wuḥūsh* (وحوش). *Ḥushirat* (حشرت) means they are gathered from every direction. Qatadah said: Everything will be gathered, even the fly, for retribution. The Mu'tazilites said: Allah, Exalted is He, will gather all animals on that day in order to compensate them for their pains which they suffered in this world through death, killing, and other things. Once they are compensated for those pains, if Allah wills to let some of them remain in Paradise when that is pleasing, He will do so; and if He wills to annihilate them, He will annihilate them, as the report has come. The sixth: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. It is read with both the light and the emphatic (tashdid) forms, and there are several interpretations of it.

The first: the root of the word is from "sajartu al-tannur" (I kindled the oven), meaning when I lit it. When a thing is kindled in it, it dries out whatever moisture is in it. Then no water at all will remain in the seas. Then the mountains will be set in motion, as He said: ﴿And the mountains are set in motion﴾. Then the seas and the earth will become one thing in extreme heat and burning. It is also possible that when the waters of the seas have dried up, the earth will swell and rise, and become level with the peaks of the mountains. It is also possible that when the mountains are crumbled and their parts scattered and become like dust, that dust falls to the bases of the mountains, so the surface of the earth becomes level with the seas, and the whole becomes a sea set ablaze (masjur).

The second: that (sujjirat) means "fujjirat" (burst forth/split open). This is because there is a barrier between the seas, as He said: ﴿He released the two seas, meeting together. Between them is a barrier which they do not transgress﴾ [al-Rahman: 19-20]. So when God removes that barrier, some of them will overflow into others, and the seas will become one sea. This is the view of al-Kalbi.

The third: (sujjirat) means "uqidat" (were kindled). Al-Qaffal said: this interpretation admits of several aspects.

The first: that Hell is in the depths of the seas. It is now not kindled, due to the continuation of this world. When the term of this world ends, God will convey the effect of those fires to the seas, and they will thereby become entirely kindled.

The second: that God Almighty will cast the sun, the moon and the stars into the seas, and the seas will thereby become kindled.

The third: that God Almighty will create great fires within the seas, until those waters become heated.

I say: these aspects are strained, and there is no need for any of them, because the One who is able to ruin this world and establish the Resurrection must certainly be able to do to the seas whatever He wills, of heating them and turning their waters into fire, without any need to cast the sun and the moon into them, or to have the fire of Hell beneath them.

Know that these six signs may occur at the beginning of the time of the ruin of this world, and they may also occur after the establishment of the Resurrection, and there is nothing in the wording that indicates one of the two possibilities. As for the remaining six, they are specific to the Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 81, verses 7–9:

The seventh: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾. On this there are several interpretations:

The first: The spirits are joined to the bodies.

The second: al-Hasan said: They will become in it three pairs, as He said: ﴿And you will be three kinds﴾ ﴿So the companions of the right hand — what are the companions of the right hand?﴾ ﴿And the companions of the left hand — what are the companions of the left hand?﴾ ﴿And the foremost, the foremost﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 8].

The third: that each category is joined with whoever was in its rank among men and women. So the outstanding in acts of obedience is joined with his like, the moderate with his like, and the people of disobedience with their like. Thus "tazwij" (pairing) means that a thing is joined with its like, and the meaning is that each one is joined to his rank in good and evil.

The fourth: Each man is joined to whoever used to accompany him of a king or ruler, as He said: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their companions﴾ [al-Saffat: 22]. It was said: then We increased them from the devils.

The fifth: Ibn 'Abbas said: The souls of the believers are paired with the wide-eyed houris (hur 'in), and the souls of the disbelievers are joined with the devils.

The sixth: Each person is joined with his sect: the Jew with the Jew and the Christian with the Christian. A marfu' report has been transmitted regarding this.

The seventh: al-Zajjaj said: The souls are joined with their deeds. Know that if you reflect on the sayings we have mentioned, you will be able to add to them whatever you wish.

The eighth: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when the buried alive girl is asked﴾ ﴿for what sin she was killed﴾. On this there are several issues:

The first issue: "wa'ada" (to bury alive) is a metathesis of "ada ya'udu" (to be heavy), "awdan" meaning he became heavy. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And it does not burden him, the preserving of them both﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255], meaning it weighs him down, because it is a weight of dust. A man, when a daughter was born to him, if he wished to let her live, would dress her in a garment of wool or hair so that she might herd the camels and sheep for him in the desert. If he wished to kill her, he would leave her until she reached a height of six spans, then he would say to her mother: "Perfume her and adorn her, so that I may take her to her relatives." He had dug a pit for her in the wilderness, and he would bring her to the pit and say to her: "Look into it." Then he would push her from behind and cover her with earth until the pit was level with the ground. It was also said: when a pregnant woman drew near her time, she would dig a hole and give birth at its edge; if she bore a girl she threw her into the hole, and if she bore a boy she kept him. Here there are two questions:

The first question: What moved them to bury the daughters? The answer: fear of the shame that would fall upon them because of them, or fear of poverty, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And do not kill your children for fear of poverty﴾ [al-Isra': 31]. They used to say: the angels are the daughters of God, so they attached the daughters to the angels. Sa'sa'ah ibn Najiyah was among those who prevented burying alive, and al-Farazdaq boasted of him in his saying:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So I swear by the stars that recede, that run and hide﴾. The discussion of "I swear" (lā uqsimu) has already been given under His saying: ﴿I swear by the Day of Resurrection﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 1]. Regarding ﴿by the stars that recede﴾ and ﴿that run and hide﴾, there are two opinions.

The first, which is the well-known one and the apparent meaning, is that they are the stars (al-nujum al-khunnas), the plural of khānis. Khunus, inqibad (contraction) and istikhfa' (concealment) all mean the same. One says: khanasa min bayn al-qawm and inkhanasa (he withdrew from among the people). In a hadith: "The Shaytan whispers to the servant, but when he remembers Allah, he withdraws (khanasa)," meaning he contracts. For this reason he is called al-Khannas. Al-kunnas is the plural of kānis and kānisah. One says: kanasa when he enters al-kinās, which is the resting place of wild animals. One says: kanasa al-zaby fi kunusihā (the gazelles hid in their lairs), and takannasat al-mar'ah when she entered her howdah, likening herself to the gazelle when it enters al-kinās.

Then the scholars differed on the receding (khunus) and hiding (kunus) of the stars in three ways.

The most evident opinion is that this refers to the retrograde motion of the five wandering planets and their return to direct motion. Given this, it is established that this Qur'an may be the speech of Jibril and not the speech of Allah. And on the assumption that it is the speech of Jibril, it falls outside being a miracle, since it is possible that Jibril delivered it to Muhammad (ﷺ) as a means of misguidance. This cannot be answered by saying that Jibril is infallible and does not commit misguidance, because knowledge of Jibril's infallibility is derived from the truthfulness of the Prophet, and the truthfulness of the Prophet is based on the Qur'an being a miracle, and the Qur'an being a miracle is based on Jibril's infallibility, so it leads to circularity (dawr), which is impossible. The answer: those who said that the Qur'an was a miracle only through ṣarfah (the doctrine that God diverted people from producing its like) went to that position in order to flee from this question, because on that view the inimitability does not lie in eloquence, but in the removal of those knowledges and motives from hearts, and that is something no one can do except Allah, exalted is He.

The second opinion: that what Muhammad told you concerning the matter of the Hour, as mentioned in this sūrah, is not soothsaying (kahānah), nor conjecture, nor fabrication. Rather, it is the word of Jibril, which he brought to him as revelation from Allah, exalted is He. Know that He described Jibril here with six attributes.

The first of them: that he is a messenger. There is no doubt that he is the messenger of Allah to the prophets, so he is a messenger and all the prophets are his community. This is what is meant by His saying: ﴿He sends down the angels with the Spirit by His command upon whomever He wills of His servants﴾ [al-Nahl: 2], and He said: ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down upon your heart﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 193].

The second: that he is noble, and from his nobility is that he gives the best of gifts, which are knowledge, guidance and direction.

[Page 68]

The third: His saying: ﴿possessor of power﴾. Some interpreted this as strength in might. It is narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to Jibril: "Allah mentioned your strength, so what have you achieved?" He said: "I lifted the four cities of the people of Lot on the pinions of my wing until the people of heaven heard the barking of dogs and the crowing of hens, and then I overturned them." Muqatil mentioned that a devil called al-Abyad, the companion of the prophets, intended to tempt the Prophet (ﷺ), and Jibril pushed him with a gentle push by which he fell from Makkah to the farthest part of India. Others interpreted it as strength in performing obedience to Allah and not failing in it from the beginning of creation to the end of the time of obligation, and as strength in knowing Allah and in contemplating the majesty of Allah.

The fourth: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿in the presence of the Lord of the Throne, firmly established﴾. This "in the presence of" (ʿindiyyah) is not a spatial presence, like His saying: ﴿and those who are with Him are not too proud﴾ [al-Anbiyaʾ: 19], nor is it a presence of direction, as shown by His saying: "I am with those whose hearts are broken." Rather, it is a presence of honor, dignity and exaltation. As for makīn (firmly established), al-Kisāʾī said: one says "so-and-so has become established (makuna) with so-and-so" with a damma on the kāf, makʾan and makānah. On this basis, al-makīn is the one of rank who gives what is asked.

The fifth: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿obeyed there﴾. Know that His saying thamma (there) points to the aforementioned place, namely ﴿in the presence of the Lord of the Throne﴾. The meaning is that he is obeyed by Allah among His near angels; they act upon His command and return to His judgment. It was read thumma (then) to magnify the trustworthiness and to clarify that it is his most excellent of the attributes enumerated.

The sixth: His saying: ﴿trustworthy﴾, meaning he is trustworthy concerning the revelation of Allah and His messages, and Allah has preserved him from treachery and error.

* * *

Then He said, exalted is He: ﴿Your companion is not mad﴾. Whoever preferred Jibril over Muhammad (ﷺ) used this verse as evidence, saying: If you weigh His saying ﴿Indeed, it is the word of a noble messenger﴾ ﴿possessor of power, in the presence of the Lord of the Throne, firmly established﴾ ﴿obeyed there, trustworthy﴾ against His saying ﴿Your companion is not mad﴾, the great difference appears. ﴿And he certainly saw him on the clear horizon﴾, meaning where the sun rises according to all, and this is explained in the sūrah of al-Najm. ﴿And he is not, concerning the unseen, withholding﴾, meaning Muhammad is not withholding concerning the unseen. The unseen here is the Qur'an and what it contains of news and stories. ḍanīn means one accused, as in "I suspected Zayd" meaning "I accused him," and it is not from ẓann (thinking) which takes two objects. The meaning is: Muhammad is not accused concerning the Qur'an, i.e., he is trustworthy in what he conveys from Allah. Whoever reads it with ḍād (ḍanīn) means it is from stinginess; one says ḍanantu bihi, adinnu, meaning I was stingy with it. The meaning is: he is not stingy regarding what Allah has sent down. Al-Farrāʾ said: the unseen of heaven comes to him, and it is a precious thing, so he does not withhold it from you. Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī said: the meaning is that he is informed of the unseen and clarifies it, and does not conceal it as the soothsayer conceals it and refuses to inform until he takes a payment (ḥulwān). Abū ʿUbaydah preferred the first reading for two reasons:

One: the disbelievers did not accuse him of stinginess; they accused him of being untrustworthy, so denying the accusation is better than denying stinginess.

Second: His saying ﴿concerning the unseen﴾. If the meaning were stinginess, it would have said bi-al-ghayb, because one says "so-and-so is stingy with such-and-such" and rarely says "concerning such-and-such."

* * *

Then He said, exalted is He: ﴿Nor is it the word of an accursed devil﴾. The people of Makkah used to say that this Qur'an is brought by a devil who places it on his tongue. Allah denied that. If it is said: the affirmation of the validity of prophethood depends on negating this possibility, so how can this possibility be negated by a transmitted (samʿī) proof? We say: we have explained that on the view of ṣarfah, the validity of prophethood does not depend on negating this possibility, and therefore it is possible to negate this possibility by a transmitted proof.

[Page 69]

Then He said, exalted is He: ﴿So where are you going?﴾ This is a rebuke to them. It is said to one who abandons the main road and goes astray: "Where are you going?" Their situation is compared to his situation in their abandoning the truth and turning away from it to falsehood. The meaning: what path are you taking that is clearer than this way which I have made clear to you? Al-Farrāʾ said: the Arabs say "to where are you going?" and "where are you going?" and they say "I went to Syria" and "I set out to the market." The people of iʿtizāl (Muʿtazilah) cited this verse as evidence, and its reasoning is evident.

Then He explained what the Qur'an is, saying: ﴿It is nothing but a reminder to the worlds﴾, meaning it is a clarification and guidance for all creatures.

Then He said: ﴿for whoever among you wills to go straight﴾. This is a substitute (badal) for "the worlds," and the sense is: "It is nothing but a reminder for whoever among you wills to go straight." The benefit of this substitution is that those who willed uprightness by entering Islam are the ones who benefit from the Reminder, as though no one else were admonished by it. The meaning is that the Qur'an is only beneficial to whoever wills to go straight. Then He explained that the will for uprightness is contingent upon the will of Allah.

﴿And you will not will except that Allah wills, Lord of the worlds﴾. That is, you will not will except that Allah, exalted is He, wills to grant you that will, because the act of that willing is a originated attribute (ṣifa muḥdatha), so its coming into being requires another will. From the totality of these verses it becomes apparent that the act of uprightness is contingent upon the will to be upright. And this will is contingent in its occurrence upon Allah's willing to grant one that will; and what is contingent upon what is contingent upon a thing is contingent upon that thing. Thus the acts of the servants, in both their establishment and their negation, are contingent upon the will of Allah. This is the position of our companions (aṣḥābunā). As for the view of some of the Mu'tazila that this verse is specific to the will of compulsion and coercion, it is weak; for we have explained that the voluntary will is a originated thing, so it requires an originator, and its coming into being is contingent upon the originator's willing to bring it into existence. In that case the objection returns. And Allah knows best what is correct.
